Calculate dissimilarity matrix for multivariate data conforming to any GLM exponential-family distribution

Source: R/glm_dist.R
glm_dist.Rd

`glm_dist()` computes a column-by-column dissimilarity matrix for a dense or sparse data matrix \(Y\) whose columns are variables and rows are observations and whose distribution conforms to any standard GLM (generalized linear model) exponential family (e.g. Poisson, Binomial, Gaussian, Gamma, Inverse-Gaussian).

Two flavours are implemented:

  • Symmetrised unit deviance (method = "deviance", default) - equal to two times the Jensen-Shannon divergence for any exponential-family distributed data. For the Gaussian(identity) family this becomes one half of the weighted squared Euclidean distance. Observation-level precision weights (e.g. Binomial totals, 1/variance for Gaussian) can be taken into account.

  • Poisson size-factor distance (method = "poissondist") - Witten (2011) distance that divides each column by its size factor before computing the symmetrised Poisson deviance, treating global scale differences as nuisance. Numerically identical to PoiClaClu::PoissonDistance(t(Y), type = "mle", transform = FALSE)$dd but computed much faster.

Usage

glm_dist(
  Y,
  weights = NULL,
  family = poisson(identity),
  method = c("deviance", "poissondist"),
  size_fac = colSums(Y)
)

Arguments

Y

A numeric matrix (`nrow(Y)` observations x `ncol(Y)` variables). Sparse `Matrix::dgCMatrix` is accepted. Proportion data should be provided in case of binomial data.

weights

Optional `nrow(Y) x ncol(Y)` matrix of precision weights (e.g. total counts for Binomial, `1/var` for Gaussian). Only used with `method = "deviance"`.

family

A **stats** family object (default `poisson(identity)`).

method

`"deviance"` or `"poissondist"` (default for family `poisson(identity)`).

size_fac

Size factors used for method `"poissondist"` (default colSums(Y), should be changed to rowSums(Y) if t(Y) is analysed to cluster rows rather than columns).

Value

An object of class **dist**.

Details

  • Symmetrised unit deviance (method = "deviance", default)
    For two columns *i* and *j* let $$\mu_t^{(i,j)} \;=\; \frac{w_{ti} y_{ti} + w_{tj} y_{tj}} {w_{ti} + w_{tj}}$$ be the precision-weighted mean at row *t*. With \(d(y,\mu,w)\) the unit deviance returned by family\$dev.resids, the distance is $$D_{ij}^{(\mathrm{dev})} = \sum_t \bigl[d(y_{ti},\mu_t^{(i,j)},w_{ti}) + d(y_{tj},\mu_t^{(i,j)},w_{tj})\bigr].$$ For the Gaussian(identity) family \(d(y,\mu,w)=w(y-\mu)^2\), hence \(D_{ij}^{(\mathrm{dev})}= \tfrac12\; \Vert y_{\bullet i}-y_{\bullet j}\Vert_2^2\), i.e. **one half of the squared Euclidean distance** (so its square-root equals Euclidean distance up to \(\sqrt{1/2}\)).

  • Poisson size-factor distance (Witten 2011) (method = "poissondist")
    With column size factors \(s_i = \mathrm{size\_fac}[i]\), row totals \(c_t = y_{ti}+y_{tj}\), and a Gamma-Poisson smoothing constant \(\beta\) (default 1), define $$n_{ti} = \frac{s_i c_t}{s_i+s_j},\qquad d_i = \frac{y_{ti}+\beta}{n_{ti}+\beta}$$ and analogously for *j*. The Witten (2011) distance is $$D_{ij}^{(\mathrm{pois})} = \sum_t\!\bigl[n_{ti}+n_{tj} - n_{ti}d_i-n_{tj}d_j + y_{ti}\log d_i + y_{tj}\log d_j\bigr].$$ Setting size_fac = rowSums(Y) yields the row-wise variant identical to PoiClaClu::PoissonDistance(x,...) without transposing *x*.

Both distances are twice the Jensen-Shannon divergence of the corresponding exponential-family distributions; for Gaussian this again equals \(\tfrac12\Vert\Delta\Vert_2^2\).

References

Witten, D. M. (2011). Classification and Clustering of Sequencing Data using a Poisson Model. Annals of Applied Statistics 5(4): 2493-2518.

Examples

## example: calculating distance among different m/z mass traces in GC/MS datasets
data(GCMS_data2) # section of a GC/MS chromatogram of beer volatiles
Y <- GCMS_data2
dim(Y) # 1764 timepoints x 518 m/z mass traces
# we aggregate together every bin of 10 subsequent timepoints for extra performance:
Y2 <- t(glm_aggregate(t(Y), 
                    family = poisson(identity), 
                    clusterids = rep(1L:ceiling(nrow(Y)/10), each=10)[1:nrow(Y)])$Y_agg)
dim(Y2) # 177 time bins x 518 m/z mass channels
D1 <- glm_dist(Y = Y2, family  = poisson(identity), method="poissondist")
# identical to D1b <- PoiClaClu::PoissonDistance(t(Y2), type = "mle", transform = FALSE)$dd
# but faster
